content: They lose the day in expectation of the night, and the night in fear of the dawn.
author: Seneca
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Courage is rarely the thunderous heroics we see in movies; it is the quiet voice at the end of the day that says, 'I will try again tomorrow.' When we wait to feel completely fearless before taking a step, we stay trapped in place.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Real strength shows up with a racing pulse and trembling hands. It is the willingness to be vulnerable, to risk looking foolish, and to stand up for what matters even when everything in you wants to hide.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
